author: @pwilkin

evidence.api_compatibility: The /files endpoint for a multi-shard model returns a different number of entries (N shards instead of 1). A client that iterated the previous response and assumed a single main-file entry may need updating. The PR author asserts no breaking change; the old behavior was arguably a bug (missing shard data), so the fix is correct, but clients with hard-coded expectations about the response shape may be surprised.
evidence.documentation: No documentation updates required per the author's checklist; the change fixes internal behavior without altering documented user-facing behavior or introducing a new feature.
evidence.manual_release_testing: The /files API behavior changed for multi-shard models: previously one entry, now one per shard. CI ran (Validate New vLLM Release, Launchpad PPA, Validate New llama.cpp Release, Docs And Style) — all passed — but no evidence of a human exercising the /files endpoint with a real multi-shard GGUF model. This is a user-visible surface change.
evidence.post_approval_commits: None. The single commit (aa8d0ced) was the head of the PR at time of merge; no commits were added after the first and latest approval on 2026-11-09T12:46:28Z.
evidence.review: One human reviewer (@fl0rianr) approved on 2026-11-09 with an LGTM. The reviewer's subject areas per docs/dev/contribute.md are LMX omni models, GUI, CI, and smart router — not gguf_shard_utils or model file inventory — so subject-matter expertise for this specific component is marginal. CodeRabbit flagged a functional-correctness issue: std::sort on shard filenames orders non-zero-padded indices lexicographically (shard 10 before shard 2), which is a real bug. The reviewer acknowledged this point but did not address it before merging, stating it was "worth addressing, but I wouldn't consider it a merge blocker."
evidence.security: No new dependencies, credential handling, network calls, or permission changes. The change is confined to file enumeration and path handling within existing code paths.
evidence.tests: New C++ unit test test_list_sharded_model_files creates a 3-shard model with zero-padded indices (model-00001-of-00003.gguf, etc.), registers it via the manager, and asserts list_model_files returns all shards with correct sizes and existence flags. An existing-shard deletion case is also covered. The Python endpoint test test_021ub_extra_subdir_sharded_size_sums_shards_but_files_stay_per_file was updated from expecting one main file to expecting two. The zero-padded test names mask the numeric-sorting bug that CodeRabbit flagged for non-zero-padded names, so the test suite does not exercise that edge case.

maintainer_todos.text: Register a multi-shard GGUF model whose shard filenames lack zero-padding (e.g., model-1-of-10.gguf, model-10-of-10.gguf), call the /files endpoint, and confirm that shard 1 appears before shard 10 in the response.

subject: fix(models): list every shard in model file inventory (#4108)
summary: For multi-shard GGUF models in extra_models_dir, the /files endpoint (via ModelArtifactStore::list_files) now enumerates every shard file instead of only the first one.
verdict_reason: All CI checks passed and the change is well-scoped, but the reviewer acknowledged a numeric-shard-sorting bug flagged by CodeRabbit without fixing it, and the change touches the /files API surface without manual release testing evidence.
